claims.text: Opioid antagonist (naltrexone) and GABA-receptor modulators (baclofen, acamprosate) appear to give short-term benefit by reducing craving and w.draw;
claims.quote: Opioid antagonists (naltrexone or nalmefene) and medications that modulate gamma-aminobutyric acid receptors (baclofen or acamprosate) appear to have a short-term benefit by reducing the craving and withdrawal symptoms.
However, evidence for disulfiram is not as strong as for other medications

claims.text: Disulfiram label: extreme caution in hepatic cirrhosis or insuff;
claims.quote: disulfiram should be used with extreme caution in patients with any of the following conditions: diabetes mellitus, hypothyroidism, epilepsy, cerebral damage, chronic and acute nephritis, hepatic cirrhosis or insufficiency.

claims.text: hepatic failure leading to transplant or death reported.
claims.quote: Hepatic toxicity including hepatic failure resulting in transplantation or death have been reported.

claims.text: Naltrexone label: stop if Sx or signs of acute hepatitis.
claims.quote: Use of naltrexone hydrochloride should be discontinued in the event of symptoms and/or signs of acute hepatitis.

claims.text: EToH w.draw requires benzodiazepines (eg, diazepam); in advanced liver dz, excessive sedation can precipitate portosystemic encephalopathy.
claims.quote: Alcohol withdrawal requires use of benzodiazepines (eg, diazepam). In patients with advanced alcohol-related liver disease, excessive sedation can precipitate portosystemic encephalopathy

claims.text: A nutritious diet and vit supplements (esp B vitamins) are important in the first days of abstinence.
claims.quote: A nutritious diet and vitamin supplements (especially B vitamins) are important during the first few days of abstinence.
